question.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type II region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le x\le {y}^{2}\}.$

So, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2y{e}^{x}\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}2y{e}^{x}\,dx\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}2y{e}^{x}\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2y[{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}{e}^{x}\,dx]dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2y[\,{e}^{x}\,]_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}2y({e}^{{y}^{2}}-{e}^{0})\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(2y{e}^{{y}^{2}}-2y)\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}(2y{e}^{{y}^{2}}-2y)\,dy & ={[{e}^{{y}^{2}}-{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =({e}^{1}-1)-({e}^{0}-0) \\  & =e-2\end{aligned}
$$
